title: dedicated-capacity-procurement-briefing
content:
Purpose: quick, procurement-facing briefing for Dedicated Capacity offers (sales enablement + RFP checklist).

Context / why this doc: we keep getting RFPs asking for: guaranteed throughput, tenant isolation, and contractable SLAs with remedies. This is a working draft to give AEs and Solutions Engineers a single-page narrative + appendix with numbers and procurement artifacts.

Target personas
- Platform engineering/ML infra buyer (primary): cares about throughput guarantees, predictable tail latencies, tenant isolation, cloud separation, and onboarding timeline.
- Procurement / legal (secondary): needs contract language, SLAs, incident reporting cadence, and data residency assurances.
- Engineering leadership / CTO (shop-level): wants predictable unit economics and migration/fallback plans.

Core positioning (elevator):
Redwood Dedicated gives your team a reserved inference fleet with contractable throughput, strict tenant isolation, and SLO-backed latency guarantees — so production LLM workloads behave like any other critical infra: predictable, auditable, and supported.

Three messaging pillars (short):
1) Predictable throughput: reserved capacity (GPU pools sized for committed concurrency), configurable autoscale bands, and per-route capacity reservations so p99 response behavior is contractable.
2) Strong isolation & compliance: VPC peering or on-prem worker nodes, customer-dedicated CUDA pools, separate key management (KMS/HSM), and no multi-tenant mixing of GPU instances.
3) Commercially reliable SLAs: uptime + latency SLOs for critical routes, formal incident playbooks, and credits/remediation for SLO breaches.

Proof points / technical hooks to back claims:
- Serving runtime: continuous batching with request prioritization; demo notes available in PR#274.
- KV cache & warm pool: cold-start mitigation strategy that preserves p99 for tail-heavy workloads.
- Kernel selection + quantization profiles: ability to tune per-customer to meet throughput targets while reducing cost.
- On-prem option: support package for air-gapped deployment and annual security review.

Competitive notes (quick takeaways for objection handling)
- vs hyperscalers (managed endpoints): hyperscalers offer scale but often lack predictable per-customer throughput guarantees and don’t provide the same level of isolation or tuned inference runtime. Emphasize our runtime + placement control.
- vs vendor X (inference hosters): X sells dedicated hardware but forces long lead times and opaque pricing. We can be faster to deploy, provide clearer cost attribution, and offer configurable autoscale.
- vs self-hosting: self-hosting gives control but requires building a production-grade serving stack (batching, autoscaler, fallback), which adds engineering cost and time. We sell the operational burden away with SLAs and dedicated support.

Procurement-ready positioning & contract language (playbook)
- Offer tiers: Bronze (committed baseline throughput, standard support), Silver (baseline + guaranteed p99 latency SLO for top N routes, faster escalation), Gold (dedicated hardware lane, X-hour RTO, named SE and SOC).
- Key contract clauses to include in template: Service Description (capacity units, region), Capacity Reservation & Right to Use, SLA & Remedies (credits tiered by duration/impact), Data Isolation & Access Controls, Incident Response & RCA timelines, Term/renewal, Termination for convenience/for cause, Security & Compliance (SOC2, ISO where applicable).
- Example SLA bullets to propose in contracts: 99.95% availability for control plane, 99% of requests served under p99 latency threshold (ms value in appendix), and 24/7 incident response for Priority 1 incidents.

Pricing guidance & commercial constructs (notes for AEs)
- Capacity units: define a "Reserved Token Throughput Unit (RTTU)" = baseline tokens/sec * hours. Price per RTTU, with usage overage at uplifted rate.
- Commitment discounts: 6/12/24 month bands with stepped discounts and optional burst credits.
- Setup/onboarding fee: one-time deployment + hardening + runbook creation.
- Optional add-ons: extended log retention, dedicated SE, on-prem consultation, enhanced response SLO.

Sales checklist (what to prepare before procurement conversation)
- Capacity runway analysis: baseline QPS, burst patterns, p99 latency target, token distribution per call. (See sample worksheet: link to product-hosted-api capacity workbook)
- Security artifacts: SOC2 report, pen-test summary, KMS architecture diagram.
- Deployment plan: timeline with milestones (pilot, rollout, go-live), rollback strategy, peak-day runbook.
- Cost model: per-RRTU pricing, amortized GPU cost, and estimated 12-month spend.

Procurement FAQ / suggested answers
Q: How do you guarantee throughput under contention?
A: Dedicated pools are isolated by tenant. We guarantee baseline capacity in the contract and provide a documented autoscale policy for burst capacity; any sustained overage is billed as overage.

Q: What are the remedies for SLA breaches?
A: Credits based on percentage of monthly fees per SLA tier; for severe breaches we offer a remediation plan and optional termination rights for repeated failures.

Q: Will our data ever be processed on shared hardware?
A: Not under Dedicated: customer-assigned worker pools are single-tenant and never host other customers’ model weights or inference contexts. For Private/on-prem deployments, all data stays on customer-managed infrastructure.

Appendix (numbers to be finalized with Eng/SRE)
- Suggested baseline SLA numbers (draft):
  * Control plane availability: 99.95% monthly
  * Data plane: 99.9% for provisioned capacity routes
  * Latency SLO: p99 <= 450ms for standard gen-1 models, p99 <= 1200ms for long-context models (depends on seq len)
  * Incident P1 response: 1 hour, P2: 4 hours, RCA within 72 hours

Conversation prep notes for AE call (short prompts)
- "Walk me through your worst-case peak day — how predictable does performance need to be?"
- "Do you require physical isolation / on-prem vs is VPC-only sufficient?"
- "What would a successful first 90 days look like for you?"

Notes-to-self / working fragments

End of briefing.
